source: A small editable library of priorities that pull against each other (MR-098). A pair fires when one priority's title carries a word from `a` and another's a word from `b`; the client confirms before it counts.

pairs.why: A beach house and a place by the slopes are two addresses; the same money and the same weekends cannot be in both.
City life and lots of land sit in different places; one home cannot be both.
A lot of travel and a pet with no sitter pull on the same weeks; the pet needs someone home.
Long trips and a garden or animals both want the same months of attention.
Stopping work early and the big-ticket wants draw on the same savings; each year of one delays the other.
A growing family and a year on the road ask for different kinds of stability.
Starting something and keeping the steady paycheck pull in opposite directions; the runway has to come from somewhere.
A simpler life and a growing collection are two answers to the same question.
Rest and a second job both want the hours after work.
Evenings with people and a climb at work both ask for the same hours.
Paying debt down and buying assets split the same surplus; one usually comes first.
Staying near family and moving away cannot both be true at once.
